hypotheses.text: Heterozygous pathogenic variants in RAB3A produce an expanded phenotypic continuum that includes hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) phenotypes alongside cerebellar ataxia, such that prominent pyramidal spasticity and hyperreflexia do not exclude a diagnosis of SCA52.
hypotheses.rationale: Prior classifications viewed SCA52 primarily as an infantile non-progressive or slowly progressive pure cerebellar ataxia resembling SCA29. However, curation updates in OMIM (#621535) and gene panels denote that RAB3A pathogenic variants also cause spastic paraplegia, directly challenging the assumption that spasticity and corticospinal tract signs rule out SCA52.

evidence.text: OMIM entry #621535 explicitly documents an expanded phenotypic spectrum for RAB3A, citing literature describing manifestations ranging from cerebellar ataxia to spastic paraplegia.

hypotheses.text: The spastic paraplegia manifestation within RAB3A-related disease is allele-specific, with distinct non-p.Arg83Trp variants or specific domain mutations causing predominant spastic paraplegia whereas switch II missense variants (p.Arg83Trp) drive slowly progressive cerebellar ataxia with vermian atrophy.
hypotheses.rationale: Resolving whether spastic paraplegia and infantile cerebellar ataxia represent allelic heterogeneity or variable expressivity of identical alleles will determine whether genotype can predict whether a patient presents with spasticity versus cerebellar signs.

evidence.text: Spinocerebellar ataxia 52 is designated as caused by heterozygous mutations in RAB3A with an expanding spectrum extending to spastic paraplegia.

hypotheses.text: SCA52 cannot be reliably differentiated from complicated hereditary spastic paraplegias (e.g., SPG7, SPG11) or autosomal dominant spastic ataxias on clinical motor examination alone, requiring neuroimaging evidence of isolated cerebellar vermian atrophy without severe spinal cord atrophy to prioritize RAB3A testing.
hypotheses.rationale: Because the phenotype includes both cerebellar ataxia and spastic paraplegia, clinicians cannot use the presence of pyramidal signs to rule out SCA52; neuroimaging biomarkers rather than bedside motor signs may be the primary discriminating clinical feature.

evidence.text: International diagnostic panels include RAB3A under gene lists for Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia in addition to spinocerebellar ataxias, reflecting overlapping diagnostic indications.

new_directions.question_text: What specific heterozygous RAB3A variant alleles have been identified in patients clinically diagnosed with hereditary spastic paraplegia versus SCA52, and do their functional effects on GTPase activity differ?
new_directions.rationale: OMIM entry #621535 highlights literature expanding RAB3A into spastic paraplegia. Pinpointing the exact alleles and biochemical consequences will clarify whether spastic paraplegia and SCA52 are allelic diseases with divergent pathogenic mechanisms.

new_directions.question_text: In patients with RAB3A-related spastic paraplegia, what is the frequency and distribution of cerebellar signs, cognitive impairment, and neuroimaging abnormalities compared to classical SCA52?
new_directions.rationale: Determining whether spastic RAB3A patients possess subclinical vermian cerebellar atrophy or oculomotor abnormalities will enable clinicians to distinguish them from other hereditary spastic paraplegias.
